Shipping containers for sale and hire across Australia

By size

Measure the ground first

More containers are ordered at the wrong length because somebody sized the load and never walked the driveway. Access rules a size out at least as often as volume does.

10ft

10ft Shipping Containers

Side access is pinched, the setback leaves nothing to manoeuvre in, or all that is needed is a lockable spot for the mower, an air compressor and a wall of hand tools.

20ft

20ft Shipping Containers

There is about seven metres of straight, reasonably level ground for it to sit on, and you would rather not discover in half a year that the bigger box was the answer.

40ft

40ft Shipping Containers

You have the space, the approach is genuinely open, and you want the most storage per dollar the site will allow.

Grade matters more than anything else in a container quote. Grade is what decides whether the box keeps water out. Anything sold as cargo-worthy is inspected wind and watertight before release — for storage use, which is separate from the CSC certification an export job needs — and new single-trip units, one loaded voyage with rubbers that have barely weathered, are sealed as well. As-is is the cheap end and carries no watertight claim at all: expect a previous repair, a floor section that has gone soft, or a gasket that no longer pulls up hard against the frame. We list those faults and photograph them on request, before delivery, so nothing turns up as a surprise when the truck does. If what goes inside has to stay dry, start at cargo-worthy.

Prices are quoted with the container and the delivery together, so the figure you get is the whole cost to your address rather than a headline that grows later. Ring 1300 467 776 or send the form and you will have a price for the exact unit.

By configuration

What the box has been set up to do

General Purpose

General Purpose Shipping Containers

The plain box, and the right call about eight times out of ten.

High Cube

High Cube Shipping Containers

Identical footprint to a standard container with another foot of height on top — 2.90m to the rail rather than 2.59m.

Side Opening

Side Opening Shipping Containers

A container with doors running the full length of one side on top of the usual pair at the end.

Refrigerated

Refrigerated Shipping Containers

Reefers — insulated panels all round, a stainless or aluminium interior, a T-bar deck for airflow, and an integral refrigeration unit built into one end.

Dangerous Goods

Dangerous Goods Shipping Containers

Storage built from the outset for flammable liquids and other dangerous goods — a bunded floor, ventilation high and low, internal shelving, and the compliance plate a workplace inspector will want to read.

Grades

Two boxes the same length can be a long way apart on price

Three grades cover nearly everything we move. The money between the top and the bottom of that range is usually larger than the gap between two yards quoting on the same grade, so settle the grade first and treat it as the only fair basis for comparing anybody's price.

The gap is almost always the floor and the door seals, and neither of them shows up in a listing that only gives you a length and a figure. Settle the grade before you start ringing around, because it is the only thing that makes two quotes comparable.

Grades explained

Common questions

Before you settle on one

How do I pick the right size?

Measure the ground before you shortlist a length. A 20ft wants roughly seven metres of straight, near-level standing and is the default because it is the size every yard and every truck is set up for. A 40ft holds about double and, on current quotes, often costs only a little more — but it will not get in anywhere without a long, clear, unobstructed approach. A 10ft exists for the block that genuinely will not take a 20ft, and it is usually the dearer way to buy room. Which is the better buy depends on the grade and the delivery run, so ask for the figures side by side.

Is a high cube worth the extra?

It buys 300mm of internal height and nothing else — 2.90m to the top rail rather than 2.59m. Left empty as a store, that foot is not worth a great deal. The moment the container is being lined, fitted with a roller door a forklift has to drive through with the tynes up, or hung with a mezzanine across one end, it is the difference between a comfortable fit-out and a compromised one. Anything being converted, buy the high cube.

Can I buy one sight unseen?

Most people do, and there is nothing wrong with it provided you are looking at the right photographs. Ask and images of the actual unit will be sent rather than a catalogue shot — corners, door end, roof and floor — on request and before delivery. If you are close enough to Cornubia to drive over, ring ahead and do that instead on used stock. Everywhere else, the photographs are the substitute and they are of your box, not a box like it.

Do you hire these as well as sell them?

Yes, across the range and into every state we deliver to. Hire suits a container with an end date attached — a build, a fit-out, a season, a shed being put back up after a storm. Buying wins the moment the box is still going to be standing there in a couple of years, because the weekly rate and the purchase price cross over sooner than most people assume. Tell us how long it is needed for and we will work out which side of that line the job sits on.

Can a container be modified?

Yes — personnel doors, windows, vents, shelving, roller doors, paint and full fit-outs. It is worth settling before you buy rather than afterwards, because the base unit you start from changes what the work costs and occasionally changes whether it is worth doing at all. A tired as-is box is cheap to buy and expensive to convert. The modifications page covers what we get asked for most often.
